plates.reference: Own code graphic: on period paper, an inked cooling-curve vs radioactive-furnace chart compares Lord Kelvin's 1862–1897 conductive cooling curve (20–40 million years without internal heat) against Earth's radiogenic heat and U-238 → Pb-206 half-life clock (4.47 billion years, with Boltwood 1907 & Holmes 1913 dating ancient rocks to 1.6 billion years).

teach_overlay.detail: Inked cooling-curve vs radioactive-furnace chart on period paper comparing Lord Kelvin's 1862–1897 conductive cooling curve (cooling to present geothermal gradient in 20–40 million years without internal heat) against Earth's radiogenic heat and U-238 → Pb-206 half-life clock (4.47 billion years, Boltwood 1907 & Holmes 1913 rocks at 1.6 billion years)
teach_overlay.scale: half of all the Uranium-238 atoms sealed inside a crystal when the Earth formed four and a half billion years ago have only just finished ticking over into lead today
